plot.explanation: Create a scientific plot from captured numeric CSV columns, explicit units, named series and linear/log10 axis ranges. Publish SVG, PNG, source capture and an editable trusted script. Optional symmetric y uncertainty draws measured intervals. Independent SVG coordinate and decoded PNG pixel checks compare actual native output with captured values. Fixed styles and connected samples only; no arbitrary commands, expressions, fits or unit conversion.
pitfalls: Replace the absolute CSV placeholder and match the exact declared header order.
Choose increasing x values, explicit inclusive ranges and matching column/axis units.
For log10, every sample and uncertainty endpoint must be positive.
Overlapping series may obscure one another and fail independent pixel identification; choose distinguishable data/colours.

examples.purpose: Measured calibration with absolute symmetric uncertainty.
Positive log10 samples with uncertainty intervals.

fields.explanation: A scientific plot document maps numeric CSV columns with declared units to connected samples and optional symmetric y error bars. Both SVG and PNG are published and independently inspected. No fitting or unit conversion is implicit.

/properties/version.explanation: Plot document contract identifier schemaxis.gnuplot/1, independent of the Gnuplot executable release.

/properties/operation.explanation: Choose plot to publish SVG and PNG together with captured CSV and an editable generated Gnuplot script.

/properties/title.explanation: Required visible plot title, at most 80 plain ASCII characters. Use letters, numbers, spaces and ._()+/-. Begin with a letter or number; quotes, backticks, percent and enhanced text are excluded.

/properties/source.explanation: Absolute path to a regular local .csv file, at most 1 MiB. Replace the starter placeholder. Exact header order must match columns; every cell must be a finite ASCII number without whitespace. Source bytes are captured and hashed before execution; changing bytes invalidates reuse.

/properties/columns.explanation: Ordered definitions of 2–12 numeric CSV columns. The first CSV row must contain exactly these distinct names in this order. Include a unit for every column; use 1 for dimensionless values.

/properties/columns/items.explanation: One named CSV column and its declared unit. Column order defines the native using index, so changing this order requires the CSV header/data to change with it.

/properties/columns/items/properties/nam.explanation: Required distinct ASCII identifier: begin with a letter, then letters, numbers or underscores, at most 40 characters. This must exactly match the CSV header and series role mapping. Display labels are authored separately.

/properties/columns/items/properties/uni.explanation: Required unit label such as s, V, mm or 1. Use consistent spelling: mapped x columns must exactly equal xAxis.unit; y and uncertainty columns must equal yAxis.unit. Units are asserted, not converted or dimensionally inferred.

/properties/series.explanation: Ordered 1–4 connected numeric series. Every label and colour must be distinct. Each series maps an increasing x column and a y column, with optional absolute symmetric y uncertainty. Multiple series may share columns.

/properties/series/items.explanation: One labelled connected series drawn with circular samples. Array order is legend and drawing order. Crossings and coincident samples can obscure pixels; independent raster verification may reject ambiguous overdraw.

/properties/series/items/properties/labe.explanation: Required distinct legend text, using the same safe ASCII alphabet as title. It identifies the series, while units belong to mapped columns and axes.

/properties/series/items/properties/x.explanation: Name of the declared column supplying horizontal coordinates. Values must increase strictly across CSV rows and fit xAxis.range. Unit must equal xAxis.unit; log10 values must be positive.

/properties/series/items/properties/y.explanation: Name of the declared column supplying vertical central values. All samples and optional uncertainty endpoints must fit yAxis.range and remain positive on log10 axes. Unit must equal yAxis.unit.

/properties/series/items/properties/erro.explanation: Optional name of the column supplying nonnegative absolute symmetric y uncertainty, in yAxis.unit. A value dy draws endpoints y-dy and y+dy; omission draws only connected samples. This is an asserted interval, not a confidence level or fitted uncertainty.
/properties/series/items/properties/erro.defaultMeaning: Omission draws connected samples without error bars.

/properties/series/items/properties/colo.explanation: Series colour: red, blue, green or purple, default red. Choose a distinct colour for every series so independent raster checks can identify its samples and connecting segments.
/properties/series/items/properties/colo.defaultMeaning: Omission selects red; other series must select distinct colours.

/properties/xAxis.explanation: Horizontal axis definition with a label, declared unit, explicit range and optional scale. Its unit must match every mapped x column. The plot occupies 15–95 percent of the image width.

/properties/xAxis/properties/label.explanation: Required plain ASCII axis name, at most 80 characters. The renderer appends the declared unit in parentheses. Choose a physical quantity such as Time or Reading; no enhanced text is interpreted.

/properties/xAxis/properties/unit.explanation: Required unit label appended to the visible axis name. It must exactly match mapped column units. Use 1 for dimensionless data. No automatic scaling, prefix conversion or dimensional analysis is performed.

/properties/xAxis/properties/range.explanation: Required [minimum, maximum] bounds in this axis unit. Use increasing finite values with separation exceeding 1e-10 relative to their magnitude. All mapped samples and uncertainty endpoints must lie inside; log10 bounds must both be positive. No autoscaling or clipping is allowed.

/properties/xAxis/properties/range/items.explanation: One finite numeric range endpoint in this axis unit, with magnitude at most 1e100. The first endpoint is the minimum and the second the maximum. Distinct increasing bounds are mandatory.

/properties/xAxis/properties/scale.explanation: Coordinate transform: linear by default, or log10 for a base-10 logarithmic axis. Log10 requires positive range bounds, samples and uncertainty endpoints. Error bars retain y-dy/y+dy meaning before this transform; log spacing is therefore asymmetric.

/properties/yAxis.explanation: Vertical axis definition with a label, declared unit, explicit range and optional scale. Its unit must match every y and uncertainty column. The plot occupies 20–90 percent of image height measured upward from the bottom.

/properties/yAxis/properties/label.explanation: Required plain ASCII axis name, at most 80 characters. The renderer appends the declared unit in parentheses. Choose a physical quantity such as Time or Reading; no enhanced text is interpreted.

/properties/yAxis/properties/unit.explanation: Required unit label appended to the visible axis name. It must exactly match mapped column units. Use 1 for dimensionless data. No automatic scaling, prefix conversion or dimensional analysis is performed.

/properties/yAxis/properties/range.explanation: Required [minimum, maximum] bounds in this axis unit. Use increasing finite values with separation exceeding 1e-10 relative to their magnitude. All mapped samples and uncertainty endpoints must lie inside; log10 bounds must both be positive. No autoscaling or clipping is allowed.

/properties/yAxis/properties/range/items.explanation: One finite numeric range endpoint in this axis unit, with magnitude at most 1e100. The first endpoint is the minimum and the second the maximum. Distinct increasing bounds are mandatory.

/properties/yAxis/properties/scale.explanation: Coordinate transform: linear by default, or log10 for a base-10 logarithmic axis. Log10 requires positive range bounds, samples and uncertainty endpoints. Error bars retain y-dy/y+dy meaning before this transform; log spacing is therefore asymmetric.

/properties/width.explanation: Image width in pixels, 640–1600, default 800. Both native SVG viewport and PNG dimensions use this value; fixed screen margins determine the data plot width.

/properties/height.explanation: Image height in pixels, 480–1200, default 600. Both outputs use this value; fixed margins leave room for title, axes and legend. No physical print size or DPI contract is implied.
